evidence.quote: Be It Enacted by the Legislature of the State of Idaho:

agora_harms: Violation of civil or human rights, including privacy

summary.short: Idaho HB 575 (2024) adds Idaho Code 18-6606, making it a crime to knowingly disclose explicit synthetic media of an identifiable person without consent, to harass or intimidate, or to extort money. Misdemeanor, or felony on a prior conviction. Effective July 1, 2024.
summary.long: Adds new Section 18-6606 to Chapter 66, Title 18, Idaho Code, creating the crime of disclosing explicit synthetic media. A person commits the offense by knowingly disclosing such media when the person knows or reasonably should know that the identifiable person did not consent and that disclosure would cause substantial emotional distress; by disclosing it with intent to annoy, threaten, harass, humiliate or degrade the person; or by possessing and threatening to disclose it to obtain money or other valuable consideration. The offense is a misdemeanor, or a felony where the person was previously found guilty of a similar offense within five years, punishable by up to ten years imprisonment, a fine of up to $25,000, or both. The text defines explicit synthetic media, identifiable individual, intimate parts, realistic, sexual conduct and synthetic media. Subsection (1)(a) does not apply to disclosures for lawful criminal investigation or prosecution, reporting unlawful conduct, public-interest matters, scientific or educational research, or civil proceedings. Interactive computer, information and telecommunication services are excluded for content provided by another person, unless the provider intentionally aids or abets the disclosure. A severability clause is included. Section 2 declares an emergency and makes the act effective on and after July 1, 2024.

"Disclose" means to make available by any means to any person.
"Explicit synthetic media" means synthetic media that depicts or appears to depict:
"Identifiable individual" means a person who is portrayed in whole or in part in synthetic media
"Intimate parts" means the nude genitals, pubic area, anus, or postpubescent female nipple.
"Realistically" means that the synthetic media is sufficiently convincing such that an ordinary person viewing the synthetic media would conclude that it is an actual image or video
"Sexual conduct" means actual or simulated sexual intercourse, oral-genital contact, manual genital contact, genital-anal contact, oral-anal contact, or other physical-genital contact.
"Synthetic media" means any image or video created or altered
"Valuable consideration" includes but is not limited to sexually explicit images or video from the identifiable individual portrayed in the synthetic media.
an interactive computer service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 230(f)(2)
an information service, as defined in 47 U.S.C. 153
a telecommunication service, as defined in section 61-121(2) or 62-603(13), Idaho Code

obligations.summary: A person shall not knowingly disclose explicit synthetic media in the three cases of subsection (1)(a) (no consent and substantial emotional distress), (1)(b) (intent to annoy, terrify, threaten, harass or degrade an identifiable person) or (1)(c) (possessing and threatening disclosure to obtain money). Section 2 sets the act's effective date as July 1, 2024.
obligations.conditional_on: Knowing conduct and one of the three listed conditions in subsection (1)(a)-(c); subsection (5) exemptions and subsection (6) service-provider limitation apply.
